prompt: Scores on a statewide test have standard deviation $\sigma = 12$ points. For random samples of $n = 36$ students, what is the standard deviation of the sample mean $\bar{x}$?
hint: Averages of many students vary less than individual scores do. By what factor does averaging shrink the standard deviation?

hints.text: Averages of many students vary less than individual scores do. By what factor does averaging shrink the standard deviation?
The formula is $\sigma_{\bar{x}} = \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}$. Here $\sqrt{36} = 6$, so divide the population value $12$ by $6$.
$\frac{12}{6} = 2$, so the standard deviation of the sample mean is $2$ points.

explanation: The standard deviation of the sample mean is $\sigma_{\bar{x}} = \sigma / \sqrt{n}$, which is smaller than $\sigma$ because averaging smooths out individual variation.
The sample size is $n = 36$ and $\sqrt{36} = 6$, so the formula gives $\sigma_{\bar{x}} = 12 / 6 = 2$.
The answer is $2$ points: means of 36 students typically fall within about 2 points of the population mean.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why divide by the square root?
steps: The mean of 36 scores is their sum divided by 36. The sum of 36 independent scores has variance $36 \sigma^2$.
Dividing by 36 divides the variance by $36^2$, leaving $\sigma^2 / 36$.
